scenes.label: LEETCODE 121 · EASY
scenes.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

items.head: THE PROBLEM
items.text: `prices[i]` is the price on day i. Buy on one day, sell on a later day. Return the best profit, or 0.

say.say: Let's run the plan on a real one: LeetCode 121, Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock.

say: You get the price for each day. Buy one day, sell on a later day, and return the best profit. For this input, it's 5: buy at 1, sell at 6.

scenes.label: STEP 1
scenes.title: Read the constraints
head: INPUT SIZE UP TO
AIM FOR
WHY
rows: Even one pass is too many steps.

say.say: The problem says up to a hundred thousand prices. A computer does about a hundred million basic steps a second.
say.show: The problem says up to 100,000 prices. A computer does about 100,000,000 basic steps a second.

say: Up to a thousand items, a loop inside a loop is fine: a million steps.

say.say: But a hundred thousand squared is ten billion steps. Too slow. So we aim for O of n.
say.show: But 100,000² is 10,000,000,000 steps. Too slow. So we aim for O(n).

say: And at a billion, even one pass is too many. That calls for O of log n.

scenes.label: STEP 2
scenes.title: Brute force first
lines: for sell from buy + 1 to n - 1:

note.text: Every buy day, every later sell day: O(n²). Slow, but correct.

say.say: Now the brute force. Start with the best profit at zero.
Try every buy day.
And every sell day after it.
Work out the profit, and keep the best one. Return it.
It's O of n squared. Too slow for the limits, but it's correct, and that matters in a minute.
say.show: It's O(n²). Too slow for the limits, but it's correct, and that matters in a minute.

scenes.label: STEP 3
scenes.title: What does each sell day need?
head: DAY

say.say: Where's the repeated work? For each sell day, the brute force rescans every earlier day.
But to sell on a given day, you only need one thing: the cheapest price before it. Keep it in one variable.

say: Then the best profit is today's price minus that cheapest price, updated as you go. One pass.

say.say: Here's the code. Start with the first price as the cheapest, and best at zero.
Walk the prices once.
Update the cheapest price so far, then the best profit if we sold today.
Return best. One loop: O of n time, and O of 1 space.
say.show: Return best. One loop: O(n) time, and O(1) space.

scenes.label: STEP 4
scenes.title: Test the edges
head: INPUT
WHY IT'S AN EDGE
ANSWER
say: Last step: the edges. One day only. Nothing to sell, so zero.

say.say: Prices that only fall. No profit, so zero, not a negative number.

wrong.head: DELETE IT
wrong.text: The fast one works on the example, so the brute force goes.

right.head: KEEP BOTH
right.text: Run both on many random inputs. Different answers? The fast one has a bug.

say.say: Here's the trap. The fast version passes the example, so you delete the slow one.
Keep it. Run both on many random inputs. If they ever disagree, the fast one has a bug. These two matched on two thousand.
say.show: Keep it. Run both on many random inputs. If they ever disagree, the fast one has a bug. These two matched on 2,000.
